chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

There occurred speech between Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn al-Hasan until the clamor arose between them, and the people gathered. So they separated that evening because of that, and I went forth in the morning regarding a need, and behold, I found Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at the door of Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and he was saying: 'O maid! Tell Abu Muhammad to come out.'

He said, 'So he came out,' and I said, 'O Abu Abdillah, what made you come so early?' He said, 'I recited a Verse from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, yesterday, so it worried me.' I said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'The Words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is His Mention: Those who join what Allah has Bidden to be joined, and have awe of their Lord, and they are fearing the evil Reckoning.'
So he said, 'You speak the truth. It is as if I never read this Verse from the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, at all.' So they both hugged and wept.

key_terms.الضَّوْضَاءُ: Clamor or loud noise indicating heated argument
key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسابِ: The evil/harsh Reckoning on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.يَصِلُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُ: Joining what Allah has commanded to be joined (kinship ties)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq use Quranic verses to resolve family disputes?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Al-Kafi* highlights the profound impact of Quranic recitation on the spiritual state of the Imams, specifically illustrating how the verse on maintaining kinship ties (*Silat al-Rahim*) prompted Imam al-Sadiq to initiate reconciliation with Abdullah ibn al-Hasan. The emotional embrace and weeping underscore the Shia scholarly view that true piety involves not just avoiding severance of ties, but actively nurturing them with humility and love, transforming potential conflict into spiritual closeness.

en.sarwar: 23. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following:

“Once a conversation took place between abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and ‘Abd Allah ibn al- Hassan and it had become quite noisy and people had gathered around. They departed from each other that evening. The next morning I was out for a task and I saw abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) at the door of ‘Abd Allah ibn al- Hassan who was saying, ‘O girl, tell abu Muhammad to come out.’

He came out and said, ‘O abu ‘Abd Allah what has made you come out this early?’ He replied, ‘Last night I read a verse of the book of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, and it worried me.’ He asked, ‘Which verse is it?’ He said, ‘It is the words of Allah, Most Glorious, Most Majestic is Whose mention, “. . . who maintain all the proper relations that Allah has commanded them to maintain, who have fear of their Lord and the hardships of the Day of Judgment,” [13:21]
He said, ‘You have spoken the truth. It seems I have never come across this verse in the book of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’ They both wept and hugged each other.’”
